title: Cast n Chill
genre: Cozy fishing sim / idle game (2D side-scrolling boat fishing with an active mode and a fully idle 'desktop' mode)
release_date: 2025-06-16 (Steam, Windows/macOS, launched during Steam Fishing Fest) [CONFIRMED – studio press release]; Nintendo Switch / Switch 2 Edition 2025-12-18 (eShop; some reports say 12-19) [CONFIRMED – Nintendo store]
early_access_date: n/a (free Steam demo from ~early May 2025, app 3686530 [CONFIRMED – Automaton 2025-05-06]; Steam Next Fest June 2025 [ESTIMATE – Next Fest round-ups])
team_size: Small team; founded in 2021 by a duo [ESTIMATE – one review/database snippet naming Brendan Watts (Ski Safari) and Mark White (Agent A, Down in Bermuda); a targeted verification search found nothing, so names and headcount are unverified]. Working assumption: 2–4 people.
developer_background: Small Melbourne studio (est. 2021) whose earlier announced project was 'Crash Course Builder' (a kart-style racer/track builder, 2023 press release, slated for 2024). Cast n Chill was described as its first PC release. Founders reportedly come from mobile hits (Ski Safari, Agent A) [ESTIMATE – unverified]. Follow-up: 'Wild n Chill' (a chill survival game; demo previewed by Aftermath; announced for Switch 2/Switch, no date).
publisher: self-published (Wombat Brawler) [ESTIMATE – press releases issued by the studio; no third-party publisher found]
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (Win/Mac): https://store.steampowered.com/app/3483740/Cast_n_Chill/ ; Demo: https://steamcharts.com/app/3686530 ; Switch: https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/cast-n-chill-switch/ ; Switch 2 Edition: https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/cast-n-chill-nintendo-switch-2-edition-switch-2/
business_model: Premium $14.99 (regular Steam discounts, e.g. 33% off); Switch 2 Edition upgrade pack; local/online 2-player via GameShare on Switch 2. No IAP found.
price_usd: $14.99 [ESTIMATE – LadiesGamers review listing US$14.99 / £12.79 / €14.79; consistent with the ~$9.9 average realised gross per copy implied by tracker revenue figures]
units_or_downloads: No official sales milestone found. Steam owner/unit estimates (mid-2026): 481.4k [Gamalytic], 495–496k [VG Insights / Sensor Tower VGI], 548.2k [PlayTracker], 333k [Vorythic], 172.2k [Raijin] — all [ESTIMATE]. Boxleiter: 8,357 reviews × 40 ≈ 334k [ESTIMATE]. Working range 250k–500k Steam units; Switch sales: no data.
peak_concurrent_players: 4,447 all-time peak on 2025-06-17 [ESTIMATE – SteamDB; SteamCharts 4,425]. Dec 2025 monthly peak 1,979 (Switch launch/holiday sale); ~250–800 concurrents in mid-2026 snapshots [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts/Steambase/Raijin]. Note: idle games keep many players connected for long sessions, so CCU is relatively high versus sales.
steam_reviews: ~8,357 reviews, ~95% positive ('Overwhelmingly Positive'), ~mid-2026 [Steam page snippet]; SteamDB ~8,288 / 94.9% (rating 91.94%); Steambase 8,139 (7,730 positive / 409 negative) [ESTIMATE – trackers].
implied_review_multiplier: n/a (no confirmed units). Tracker-implied ≈ 58–60 (Gamalytic 481k / VGI 496k ÷ ~8.3k reviews) vs ≈ 21 (Raijin 172k ÷ 7.8k). I used 40 (default premium indie) for the central estimate.
gross_revenue: Steam ≈ $2.5M–$4.9M lifetime to ~mid-2026 [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter 334k × $14.99 × 0.75 ≈ $3.75M central; Sensor Tower/VG Insights $4.9M; Raijin $1.7M (lowest)]. Switch revenue: no data.
net_revenue: Steam ≈ $1.6M–$3.2M (central ≈ $2.4M) [ESTIMATE – gross × 0.70 (under $10M) × 0.93]. Self-published, so this goes to the studio (assuming no publisher).
production_cost: No disclosed figure. ≈ $150k–$400k [ESTIMATE – 2–4 people × ~18 months × ~$6k/month (Australia lean indie)]; studio founded 2021, demo May 2025, launch June 2025.
development_time: no data [CONFIRMED figure]; ≈ 1–2 years [ESTIMATE – Steam app 3483740 created ~early 2025; demo May 2025; launch June 2025; studio active since 2021 on other projects].
why_popular: A 'cozy + idle' fishing game with gorgeous detailed pixel art (day/night, weather, seasons, snowmobile ice-fishing in winter areas). Two modes: active cast-and-reel or a fully idle mode where the game fishes for you, so it lives on a second monitor or desktop while you work, study or game (the same desktop-companion trend as Rusty's Retirement, Bongo Cat and Ropuka's Idle Island). It is low-stress, ASMR-ish and relaxing ('for those that need to kick back'), with a satisfying collection/upgrade loop (rods, boats, new spots, fish log) and a companion dog. It launched into Steam Fishing Fest for algorithmic visibility, and the idle-game boom of 2025 drove discovery.
marketing_channels: Steam demo (May 2025) with strong reception covered by Automaton/Aftermath; Steam Next Fest (June 2025); launch timed to Steam Fishing Fest (2025-06-16); idle/desktop-companion curation and PC Gamer-style idle round-ups; cozy-game YouTube/TikTok/Reddit communities (pixel-art GIFs); seasonal Steam sales; Nintendo Switch / Switch 2 port at Christmas 2025.
art_style: High-detail 2D pixel art, side-scrolling, with layered parallax backgrounds, weather/day-night lighting and a cozy palette
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the whole loop (casting/reeling minigame, fish spawn tables by spot/weather/time, idle auto-fish mode, upgrades/economy, save system, a transparent/always-on-top or small-window desktop mode, Steam achievements); generate placeholder fish/props icons and backgrounds (Retro Diffusion/PixelLab are good for pixel art); SFX/ambience (ElevenLabs); lo-fi music (Suno/Udio); fish descriptions. | AI cannot: match Cast n Chill's hand-polished parallax pixel art and animation quality at a consistent, pro level (budget for a pixel artist or heavy manual cleanup); tune the 'chill' pacing and idle economy; playtest; build a cozy-community audience. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 (GodotSteam) or Unity + Steamworks.NET; Retro Diffusion / PixelLab / Aseprite for pixel art; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno lo-fi tracks.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 2–4 weeks, $150–$400 (Claude Pro/Max, pixel-art AI tool $10–$30, Steam Direct $100). Excludes the developer's own living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 3–6 months, $2,000–$8,000 (subscriptions, freelance pixel-art polish/animation $1,000–$5,000, music licensing or commission, macOS notarisation $99/yr, festival/marketing budget). Excludes living costs.

data_conflicts: Units: Gamalytic 481k / VGI 496k / PlayTracker 548k vs Vorythic 333k vs Raijin 172k (a 3× spread); I used a 250k–500k range with ~334k Boxleiter central. Revenue: $1.7M (Raijin) vs $4.9M (Sensor Tower/VGI). Peak CCU: 4,447 (SteamDB, 2025-06-17) vs 4,425 (SteamCharts); Raijin's '1,979 all-time peak' is actually the Dec 2025 monthly peak. Switch date: 12-18 (eShop) vs 12-19 (Nintendo Everything), probably time zones. Team/founder names (Brendan Watts, Mark White) come from a single unverified snippet. Price: $14.99 is from a review listing, not the Steam page directly.
notes: The most direct comparable for How to Fish: a fishing theme with a cozy/idle twist reached roughly 250k–500k Steam units at $14.99 with ~4.4k peak CCU and ~95% positive reviews, without any multiplayer virality. Its levers: (1) a desktop-idle mode, so people keep it running and it 'charts'; (2) top-tier pixel art that sells itself in GIFs; (3) launching into the Steam Fishing Fest themed sale; (4) a Switch 2 port for the holidays. For a solo+AI creator, an idle fishing game is among the most feasible builds; the main investment is art quality, so budget for a pixel artist. Combining How to Fish's co-op physics comedy with Cast n Chill's idle/desktop mode is an untested but plausible hybrid.
